question: Did the risk of a motorist being killed per mile driven in NYC decline from 2013 to 2025? Make a chart and answer based on this crash data.

options.metric: Annual sum of number_of_motorist_killed (recorded motorist deaths) in police-reported NYC crashes dated 2013–2025.
options.reason: It directly shows the annual recorded fatality burden without implying an exposure-adjusted risk.
options.answer: This dataset cannot establish whether per-mile risk declined; annual recorded motorist deaths numbered 110 in 2013 and 81 in 2025.
options.interpretation: This file cannot answer whether risk per mile declined because it contains no miles-driven denominator. The chart sums number_of_motorist_killed across police-reported NYC crashes by crash calendar year (2013–2025), showing 110 recorded motorist deaths in 2013 and 81 in 2025; annual counts are a defensible measure of recorded fatality burden but do not adjust for travel exposure. It leaves deaths per mile unanswered. The check found 0 NULL crash dates and 0 missing motorist-death values, with January 1–December 31 coverage in every selected year, so I kept all plan-year rows (excluding years outside 2013–2025) and neither excluded nor separately grouped rows for those missing fields.

options.metric: Annual number_of_motorist_killed divided by annual police-reported crash rows, expressed as recorded motorist deaths per 100,000 crashes.
options.denominator: All police-reported crash rows in that calendar year, including rows with zero motorist deaths.
options.reason: It normalizes the annual death count by the volume of crash records and reports an outcome frequency per recorded crash.
options.answer: This dataset cannot establish whether per-mile risk declined; recorded motorist deaths per 100,000 crash rows were 53.99 in 2013 and 94.69 in 2025.
options.interpretation: This file cannot answer whether risk per mile declined because it contains no miles-driven denominator. The chart sums number_of_motorist_killed in each crash year and divides by all police-reported crash rows that year (including zero-death crashes), expressing the result per 100,000 crashes; this is a defensible crash-record-normalized outcome frequency, not personal or travel-exposure risk.
